question: Should OpenClaw make `gateway.restore.status` and the restored-admission startup handoff part of the supported Gateway/core contract now, or keep those responsibilities host-owned until the RFC defines a narrower seam?
rationale: The branch is deliberately an implementation proof for a new cross-boundary recovery lifecycle; source review cannot choose the permanent public protocol and startup ownership policy safely.

options.title: Approve a narrow core contract
options.body: Sponsor the read-only restore-status method and an explicitly documented startup handoff, then require the environment carrier to be replaced or formally approved.

options.title: Keep recovery observation host-owned
options.body: Remove the public RPC and core startup carrier, retaining only any internally justified primitives that fit existing owner boundaries.

options.title: Defer pending RFC resolution
options.body: Pause this stack until the RFC records the accepted ownership split and required compatibility guarantees.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core contract
recommendation.body: Sponsor the read-only restore-status method and an explicitly documented startup handoff, then require the environment carrier to be replaced or formally approved.
